before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Wonderful. Which page explains that leftover door?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Could you hold it for a second?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Certainly. Just to clarify: you're asking for my help?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Right, I'll get this cupboard standing straight. Pass me the instructions and we'll sort it out.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I can read them. I only need someone to hold the door.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Excellent. You read; I'll manage the holding. Tell me where you want my hands.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Here, while I put the hinge in. Don't move until I say.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Perfect. I'll keep it steady under your direction. That means you do need me for this bit, doesn't it?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've brought a blanket. Your heater's still broken? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm managing. Leave the blanket, though.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Gladly. Would you say you needed my help?

before.speaker: B
before.text: I need the blanket. I can reset the heater myself.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Of course. The fuse box is in my locked cupboard. Shall I wait while you manage?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've brought the blanket. We'll get you warm first, then I'll supervise the heater reset.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I know how to reset it. Could you just leave the blanket?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Of course. I'll take care of warmth, you take care of the switch. That's the sensible division.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Actually, could you hold the blanket round me while I reach behind the heater?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Certainly. You direct the reset; I'll keep this tucked in. Just say you need my hands here, and I won't move them.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you get your train, could you taste this soup? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It needs salt.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll fix that. You'll need to check again.

before.speaker: B
before.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Perfect. That's when the bread comes out.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll get lunch right before your train. Taste this soup and I'll make the final adjustment.

after.speaker: B
after.text: It needs salt, but I haven't time for a whole bowl.

after.speaker: A
after.text: One spoonful will do. I'll season just that and you can give me the verdict.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'll take it in a flask. I really must go.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Excellent plan. Hold the flask while I pour, then check one drop from the lid. I won't send you off with a lunch you haven't signed off on.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you zip your suitcase, let me wrap that jar of jam. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. That's your train jumper. We'll need to unpack it and find something else.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll leave the jam here.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Then you haven't tasted it. I'll get a spoon before you decide.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll finish your packing. Give me the jam jar and I'll wrap it properly before you close the case.

after.speaker: B
after.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper. I need to leave.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Good thinking. I'll tuck the sleeves round the lid; just check the glass with me so we know it won't leak.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'd rather leave the jar here than keep fussing with it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Sensible. I'll look after it. Have one taste from a spoon before you decide it's mine to keep; you can tell me whether I should save you another jar.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've put your usual mug out. We can still have tea. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm hoping you won't leave me cross.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Could you try one where you're sorry about yourself? I'll keep the tea warm.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've set out our mugs. We'll put this right over tea and have a pleasant afternoon.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Are you cross with me? I don't want another argument.

after.speaker: A
after.text: No argument. You can take your time; I'd just like to hear that you're sorry before I pour.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'm sorry you're upset. Is that enough?

after.speaker: A
after.text: It's a start. I'll pour while you try the part about yourself. Just one sentence, and we can have the afternoon I promised.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your parents arrive in ten minutes. I'd like to be able to smile at you. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I thought we'd sorted this out by text.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You sent a thumbs-up. I couldn't hear any remorse.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll send a sad face.

before.speaker: A
before.text: You're right here. Could you give the sad face a sentence beginning with 'I'?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Your parents arrive in ten minutes. I'll get us smiling before they ring; we only need to finish one small conversation.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I thought we'd finished it by text.

after.speaker: A
after.text: The thumbs-up was a useful start. Give me the words that go with it and I'll call us ready.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I can send a sad face if that helps.

after.speaker: A
after.text: It does. Keep the phone down and give me that face with a sentence starting 'I'm sorry.' Quietly is fine; I just need to hear it before I open the door.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Would you support a small improvement to the front garden? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: What sort of improvement?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Something with a pond. And no tree.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Where's the tree?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Let's finish agreeing before the stump grinder leaves.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've got the garden improvement under control. A little pond will make the front look lovely, if you're happy with it.

after.speaker: B
after.text: What about the tree? I like the shade.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've arranged a bench with a canopy. You can choose where it goes; I want your shady corner kept.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Why are you replacing the tree's shade? Where is it?

after.speaker: A
after.text: It's been cut down. I'll stop the grinder until you've chosen what happens next. If I keep that corner shaded exactly as you want, can we call the pond a good decision?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. How do you feel about me inviting a few people to dinner? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Tonight? We have two chairs.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. So standing guests would be more considerate?

before.speaker: B
before.text: How many people?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Six. I've already invited them. Would borrowing enough chairs for everyone turn that into a yes?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll manage dinner tonight. A few guests will be lovely, provided you're with me on it.

after.speaker: B
after.text: We only have two chairs. I don't want people standing round my plate.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then everyone gets a seat. I'll borrow the chairs and you can choose the table arrangement.

after.speaker: B
after.text: How many have you asked already?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Six. I've sent the invitations. I'll do the fetching and the washing-up as well; can you give me a yes on the dinner if the seating is yours to settle?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. These eighty wedding place cards need names. Your bin labels have better lettering than our invitations. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I like calligraphy. I hate copying guest lists.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'd read the names. You'd only do the beautiful part.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'll handle my aunt. The ink colour could be entirely yours.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll have these eighty wedding cards finished tonight. Your lettering would make them worth keeping; would you take the pen?

after.speaker: B
after.text: I like lettering. I don't want to copy a guest list all evening.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Good. I'll read every name to you. You can make each card look exactly as you like.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Even purple? Your aunt will make you ask me to change it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Purple is now my color scheme. I'll tell her that before she sees them. Will you start with her name while I read it out?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You have such a good eye for storage. Sorting our shed could finally give your tools a proper home. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Until you dump paint tins everywhere again.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You could assign every shelf. I'd follow your labels.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Including a shelf you're forbidden to touch?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Absolutely. You could put it at eye level so I see what I'm missing.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'm getting this shed organized. Your tools deserve proper shelves; would you like to decide where everything belongs?

after.speaker: B
after.text: Only until you dump paint tins wherever you like.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then I'll carry the tins and you assign their places. I'll follow the labels; that will be our system.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Including a shelf you're not allowed to touch?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Absolutely. I'll announce that rule myself. Pick the shelf you want protected, and I'll clear it first if you'll take on the rest.
